description: validate_script recurses with a depth counter and returns an error at depth >= MAX_VALIDATE_DEPTH (32). This matches Dovecot Pigeonhole's limit. Without this, a malicious script with 10000 nested if blocks would exhaust the stack during compile(). The test 'deeply_nested_if_blocks_rejected' validates the limit at compile-time. Note: the evaluator (eval_stmt, eval_if) does NOT have a corresponding depth limit -- deeply nested scripts that somehow bypass compile-time validation (or future changes to compile()) would stack-overflow at eval time. This asymmetry should be documented.
title: good: sieve-native validate_script enforces MAX_VALIDATE_DEPTH=32 to prevent stack overflow
